messages:
sam: Quick design sync  tradeoff between dense scorecard rows vs more explicit inline confirmations for Prompt Evals. Prototype: https://files.redwood/s/scorecard-v2. Main questions: should approve/mark-regression be inline pills or tucked behind a hover menu, and do we require a quick inline confirm for single approvals? Need product + a11y + eng input before we freeze layout.

elaine: Dense rows win for skimming, but inline confirm (small popover: 'Approve? Confirm' ) reduces accidental approvals. Visually the confirm adds weight and pushes density down. Option: require confirm only for bulk approve, single-click for individual rows with undo toast.

jon: From implementation cost: inline popovers are fine but increase event handlers and DOM complexity. Undo toast is cheapest (no modal). However undo needs reliable optimistic updates and background rollback logic. We should prefer toast+undo for single approvals and require confirm for bulk operations.

maya: From usability tests, accidental single approvals are frequent when users misclick. Users prefer immediate action + easy undo rather than extra confirmation. So toast+undo aligns with user expectation. For bulk actions, a confirm modal that shows count and sample items is safer.

aria: A11y notes:
- If we use an inline confirm popover, ensure it is keyboard-trappable and focus is moved into it. Provide clear labels: 'Confirm approve' not just 'Confirm'.
- Undo toast must be reachable via keyboard and announced with aria-live="assertive": 'Result approved. Undo.'
- Bulk confirm modal must have role="dialog" and aria-labelledby for the heading 'Confirm bulk approve'. Include item count in the heading.
- Visual: keep tap targets >= 44px and ensure contrast of the undo link/button.

sam: Summarizing decisions for handoff:
1) Single-row: one-click approve with optimistic update + undo toast (aria-live assertive) for rollback.
2) Bulk approve: modal confirm listing count and first 3 items; keyboard-trappable dialog.
3) Actions: show primary 'Approve' pill visible on row hover/focus; secondary kebab for less common actions.
4) Accessibility: toast undo focusable, modal labelled, and ensure tab order includes action pills before next row.

elaine: I'll update mocks: dense rows with hover-revealed pill, toast pattern, and bulk confirm modal layout. Will also produce an expanded keyboard flow diagram. ETA: EOD.

jon: I'll prototype optimistic approve + undo API flow and ensure no layout shifts when toast appears. ETA: tomorrow noon.

aria: I'll draft an a11y test checklist for both flows and run it against the updated prototype.

assets-bot: uploaded files: scorecard_v2_dense.png, bulk_confirm_modal.sketch (https://files.redwood/s/scorecard-v2)

sam: Thanks team 44D. Action owners: @elaine mocks, @jon spike, @aria a11y checklist. Flag any blockers before the sprint freeze.
